newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes steady in modest Gulf activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes steady in modest Gulf activity.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices steadied Friday morning in modest trading, leaving outright and cash grade differentials even from Thursday.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood even at $20.05-10 a barrel, with the September/October spread hovering around -21/19 cents.

Dealers in the Gulf said many players were absent from trading rooms, leaving a scarcity of offers for some sectors. There were trades for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 22 cents over benchmark, and Midland/WTI at 30 cents under WTI.
Sour prices saw West Texas Sour/Midland climb to a $1.25 discount against the marker, and then fall back to a trade at $1.32 under WTI.
Other prices were steady from Thursday, notably in the Postings business where sales hit at $1.85/1.87/1.90.
Outright prices appeared to be in a consolidative mode, though support continued to run high from the gasoline market, where prompt prices peaked higher by midday.
